title: How to mute a thread in Apple Mail on Mac: toolbar and Message menu steps
metaTitle: How to Mute a Thread in Apple Mail on Mac (Step by Step)
description: Learn how to mute a thread in Apple Mail on Mac, with the Mute button or Message menu, what the mute icon means, and how to fix alerts that still ring.
targetKeyword: how to mute a thread in apple mail on mac
intro: To mute a thread in Apple Mail on Mac, select the conversation, then click Mute in the Mail toolbar, or choose Message > Mute from the menu bar. A muted conversation stays in your Inbox, and new messages in it make no sound and no notification.
tldr: Select the conversation in the message list, then click Mute in the Mail toolbar.
If Mute is hidden, click More Toolbar Items. Or use Message > Mute from the menu bar.
Muting silences new alerts for that one thread. The thread stays in your Inbox.
A mute icon appears on the thread's messages. Apple does not describe the icon's look.
If a muted thread still alerts, check Notifications and Focus for Mail in System Settings.

blocks.text: Muting is a switch for one conversation. You use it when a single email thread keeps pinging you and you do not want to silence Mail as a whole. The conversation stays where it is. You can still open it and read it. What changes is the alert. New messages in a muted thread make no sound and no notification. That makes mute the right tool for a long group chain, a vendor who writes every hour, or a thread you no longer need to follow closely.
Mute a thread in Apple Mail on Mac, step by step

The steps use the Mail toolbar first, because Apple's Mail guide for macOS Sequoia lists the button there. Apple's Canadian guide and a 2024 Sonoma guide use the Message menu. Both routes end at the same command. Pick the one that shows up on your screen.
Where the Mute button sits in the Mail toolbar

The toolbar is the row of buttons across the top of the Mail window. Mute appears there after you select a conversation. Some people hide toolbar items to clear space, and if you did, Mute may be out of sight. Click More Toolbar Items to find it. Apple's guide describes this fallback, so try it first when the button seems missing.
Use the Message menu instead

items: Click the conversation once in the message list to select it.
Click Message in the menu bar at the top of the screen.
Click Mute in the Message menu.
To unmute later, select the conversation, click Message, then click Unmute.

blocks.text: The menu bar route takes one more click than the toolbar. It also shows the command in words, which helps when a toolbar icon is unclear. Both routes change the same setting for that conversation, so you can switch between them as you like.
What the mute icon looks like

After you mute a thread, a mute icon appears on the messages in that conversation in the message list. Apple's guide says so. It does not describe what the icon looks like, so look at the messages and compare them with a thread you have not muted. A 2019 How-To Geek guide describes a bell with a dash through it for muted items. That article names macOS Catalina but does not say its steps were tested there. Treat the bell as a clue, not a promise.
What muting does and does not do

items: New messages in the muted thread make no sound and no notification.
The conversation stays in your Inbox, so you can still open it.
Other conversations keep their normal alerts.
Apple's guide does not say how muting changes unread counts, so check that yourself.

blocks.text: Muting is not the same as blocking. A block stops a sender's mail from reaching you, which is a bigger step. The [block a sender guide](/how-to/block-a-sender-in-apple-mail) covers that route. Use mute when the sender is fine and the thread is the problem.
Worked example: muting a vendor thread

Say a shipping vendor has sent a long chain about one order, and every reply pings your Mac. Click the conversation once. Click Mute in the toolbar, or use Message > Mute. The thread stays in your Inbox, and new replies in it stop chiming. Your other threads still alert you as usual. When the order closes, select the thread and click Unmute if you want alerts again.

Notice what you did not change. You did not edit an account setting, and you did not turn off Mail. That is the point of a per-thread mute. It keeps the rest of your mail working the way it did before.
Keep muted threads out of your Inbox

Apple's guide describes a General settings option that can move muted conversations to an archive or trash mailbox. It uses whichever of those is available for the account. Apple does not give the option's exact label, so read the General pane carefully. Open Mail > Settings, or press ⌘, then choose General. Look for a choice about muted conversations.
Think before you turn it on. A muted thread that moves out of the Inbox is easy to miss. Decide whether you want that for every account, or only for the ones that send you the most noise.
Pick the right tool: mute, notifications, or Focus
Mute is one of several ways to quiet Mail. The others act on more than one thread. Use the smallest tool that fixes your problem, and check the table below.

blocks.text: Why a muted thread still makes a sound

Mute covers one conversation. If you still hear alerts from that thread, a wider setting is probably allowing them. Start with System Settings > Notifications > Mail. Apple's notification guide says that turning off Allow Notifications for Mail stops all Mail notifications. That is useful if you want silence across the app, and too blunt if you do not.

Next, check your Focus. Apple's notification guide says a Focus must allow Mail notifications to show. Focus filters can also limit which accounts send notifications, so check them if one account is quieter or louder than you expect.
Keyboard shortcuts for muting

Apple's Mail keyboard shortcut table lists shortcuts for reply, archive and mark as read. It does not list a shortcut for muting or unmuting, so the toolbar and the Message menu are the documented routes. Shortcuts that work with a selected thread include Reply ⌘R and Archive ⌃⌘A. Some third-party guides describe assigning your own shortcut in System Settings. Apple's Mail documentation does not cover that path, so test it before you rely on it.
Common mistakes with muted threads

items: Turning off all Mail notifications when only one thread is noisy.
Looking only in the toolbar, when Mute may sit in the Message menu or behind More Toolbar Items.
Forgetting the General setting that moves muted threads out of the Inbox.
Assuming Focus is off because the thread is muted. Focus is a separate setting.
Expecting a bell icon. Apple does not describe the icon, so compare the messages yourself.

blocks.text: Version differences: Sequoia, Sonoma and macOS 27

The toolbar steps on this page come from Apple's Mail guide for macOS Sequoia 15. The Message menu route appears in Apple's Canadian guide and in a Mac Sales guide for Sonoma, published July 16, 2024. Apple's Mail User Guide now lists macOS 27 Golden Gate first. The mute page this page relies on is the Sequoia version, so the macOS 27 location is not confirmed here. Check the toolbar first, then the Message menu.
How much email muting can help

Mute helps most when the noise is constant. Microsoft's Work Trend Index says the average worker receives 117 emails a day. Most of those are skimmed in under 60 seconds, according to the same page. Those numbers describe volume, not one bad thread.

Microsoft also reports that Microsoft 365 employees are interrupted every two minutes during core work hours, 275 times a day. That figure covers the top 20% of users by ping volume, so it is not an average. Read it as a sign of how noisy a busy day can get.

Muting one thread will not fix a day like that. It removes one source of noise, and it gives you a simple test for the next thread. Ask whether the thread needs your attention every time. If the answer is no, mute it.
Next steps after you mute a thread

If one sender is the real problem, block them instead of muting every thread. If a whole stream of mail should skip the Inbox, a rule may fit better. See [how to create a rule in Apple Mail](/how-to/create-a-rule-to-sort-incoming-mail-in-apple-mail). For mail you always want to see, the [VIP mailbox guide](/how-to/use-the-vip-mailbox-in-apple-mail) keeps those senders in one place.
If you send a lot of mail yourself, the [scheduled send guide](/how-to/schedule-an-email-to-send-later-in-apple-mail) shows how to control timing on your side of a conversation.

faq.question: Does muting a thread in Apple Mail delete it?
faq.answer: No. Apple's guide says a muted conversation stays in your Inbox. If a thread disappears, check the General setting that moves muted conversations to an archive or trash mailbox.

faq.question: Why is the Mute button missing from my Mail toolbar?
faq.answer: The toolbar may have been customized, or Mute sits past the visible area. Click More Toolbar Items to find it. The Message menu has the same Mute command.

faq.question: Is there a keyboard shortcut to mute a thread in Mail on Mac?
faq.answer: Apple's Mail keyboard shortcut table does not list one for muting or unmuting. Use the Mute button in the toolbar, or choose Message > Mute.

faq.question: Will I still get notifications from other threads after I mute one?
faq.answer: Yes. Muting covers one conversation. Other threads keep their alerts, unless Mail notifications are off in System Settings or a Focus blocks them.

faq.question: What do I do if a muted thread still makes a sound?
faq.answer: Open System Settings > Notifications > Mail and check Allow Notifications. Turning it off stops all Mail alerts. Then check whether a Focus is blocking Mail.

faq.question: Can I mute a thread in the iCloud.com web app?
faq.answer: This page does not confirm a mute option in iCloud.com. Apple's mute steps cover Mail on the Mac, so use the Mac app for this task.

faq.question: Does the bell icon from older guides still appear?
faq.answer: Not confirmed. A 2019 How-To Geek guide describes a bell with a dash for muted items, but Apple does not describe the icon. Compare the icon on a muted thread with an unmuted one.

task: Mute a thread in Apple Mail on Mac
appliesTo: Apple Mail on Mac: Sequoia 15 toolbar steps and the Message menu route
requirements: A Mac with Apple Mail set up and at least one account added
The conversation you want to mute, with the message list visible
Access to the Mail toolbar or the Message menu in the menu bar

steps.name: Select the conversation
steps.text: Open Mail and go to the mailbox that holds the thread, usually Inbox. Click the conversation once in the message list so it is highlighted. Mute works on the whole conversation, not on one message inside it.
steps.tip: Select the thread row itself so the toolbar acts on the conversation you want.

steps.name: Click Mute in the toolbar
steps.text: Look at the toolbar across the top of the Mail window. Click Mute. Apple's guide for macOS Sequoia 15 describes this button.
steps.tip: If you do not see Mute, click More Toolbar Items and choose Mute from there.

steps.name: Or use the Message menu
steps.text: Click Message in the menu bar at the top of the screen, then click Mute. This is the same command as the toolbar button. Apple's Canadian guide lists this route.
steps.tip: Use this route when the toolbar is full or has been customized.

steps.name: Check for the mute icon
steps.text: Scan the messages in the thread in the message list. A mute icon should now appear on them. Apple's guide does not describe the icon, so compare it with an unmuted thread.
steps.tip: If the Message menu now shows Unmute, the thread is already muted.

steps.name: Unmute when you want alerts back
steps.text: Select the muted conversation. Click Message, then click Unmute. In the toolbar version, click the Unmute button instead, since Apple's guide says unmute works the same way.
steps.tip: Muting keeps the conversation in your Inbox, so there is nothing to recover when you unmute.

troubleshooting.problem: Mute button is missing from the toolbar
troubleshooting.fix: Click More Toolbar Items in the toolbar to find Mute, or use Message > Mute from the menu bar. Both run the same command.

troubleshooting.problem: A muted thread still makes a sound
troubleshooting.fix: Open System Settings > Notifications > Mail. If Allow Notifications is on, Mail alerts are allowed, so check Focus next. Apple's guide says turning Allow Notifications off silences all Mail notifications.

troubleshooting.problem: A muted thread disappeared from the Inbox
troubleshooting.fix: Open Mail > Settings, then General, and check the option that moves muted conversations to an archive or trash mailbox. Apple does not give the option's exact label, so read the choices before you change them.

troubleshooting.problem: Mail alerts stop even for threads you want
troubleshooting.fix: Check System Settings > Notifications > Mail. Allow Notifications off stops every Mail alert, muted or not. Turn it back on, then check whether a Focus is blocking Mail.

troubleshooting.problem: Cannot find a mute option on iCloud.com
troubleshooting.fix: This page does not confirm a mute option in the iCloud.com web app. Apple's mute steps cover Mail on the Mac, so use the Mac app for this task.
